## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Supattajātaka* (Ja 292) is a canonical birth-tale in the *Jātaka* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It has been translated into English under the title *Fairwing the Crow King* [SuttaCentral]. The canonical text opens with the verse phrase *Bārāṇassaṁ mahārājā* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].
According to the background narrative in the commentary, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at Jetavana concerning the nun Bimbādevī (Rāhulamātā) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879; Ratanamalai 2007]. When she suffered from an abdominal wind ailment (*udaravāta*), she was cured by a special meal of fine rice blended with fresh ghee and seasoned with red fish (*rohitamaccha*), which was provided by the Elder Sāriputta after her son, the novice Rāhula, sought assistance on her behalf [Fausböll 1879; Ratanamalai 2007]. The commentary notes that this contextual setting mirrors the narrative background of the *Abbhantarajātaka* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].
In terms of parallels and textual relationships, SuttaCentral registers a parallel in Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit in the *Mahāvastu* (Mvu 76, *The Jātaka of the Crow*) [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text reuse from DharmaNexus shows extensive alignment within the Pali tradition with the prose *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), including matching text across segments §0.4–3.4 [DharmaNexus].
